task: If I deploy a new recommender model via canary, what should I monitor to detect drift? Cite your sources.
final_answer: During canary rollout of a new recommender model, monitor four categories in parallel: (1) **Input drift** — feature distributions using PSI (flag > 0.1, alarm > 0.25), KS tests for continuous features, chi-square for categoricals [doc2_model_monitoring.md]; (2) **Output drift** — prediction/confidence distributions, to catch concept drift when labels aren't yet available [doc2_model_monitoring.md]; (3) **Guardrail metrics** — business KPIs that shouldn't regress even if the target metric improves (e.g. revenue shouldn't drop while CTR rises) [doc3_ab_testing.md]; (4) **Operational metrics** — latency, throughput, error rate [doc2_model_monitoring.md]. Compare the canary arm against the control arm, not against a historical baseline, so you isolate the effect of the new model [doc5_model_deployment.md].

hits.text: Population Stability Index (PSI) is a common metric for detecting drift in individual features. PSI values above 0.1 suggest moderate drift; above 0.25 suggest significant drift.
Kolmogorov-Smirnov tests compare the cumulative distributions of two samples and are useful for continuous features. Chi-square tests work well for categorical features...

Operational metrics (latency, throughput, error rate) are necessary but not sufficient. You also need input monitoring (feature distributions, missingness, schema violations), output monitoring (prediction distributions, confidence distributions), and quality monitoring...
